chunks: Al-Kafi: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a matter so he answered me, then a man came to him and asked him about it so he answered him with a different answer to mine, then another man came…
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam give different answers to the same question from different people?
ai.summary: This narration from the Book of Al-Kafi illustrates the concept of differing answers (ikhtilaf) in hadith transmission. The narrator (Zurara) asks Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) a question, receives an answer, and then observes that when other men ask the same question, the Imam provides different answers, highlighting the context-dependent nature of religious rulings.
